author: Michael Wiggins De Oliveira
title: Apple: Irrational Fear - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Investment Thesis Apple ( AAPL ) has had a turbulent 2018, with its share price not advancing since the start of the year. Although, operationally, Apple continues to make strong progress.
Apple's Services business will soon be recognized for being the crown jewel amongst a portfolio already laden with diamonds. Yet for now, investors remain dispassionate towards Apple, leaving its share price trade at a great bargain price.
Recent Developments For a long time, Apple has not seen its share price sell-off as swiftly as it has in the past 2 months. Investors are most likely looking around at other high-flying tech stocks, such as Netflix ( NFLX ) or Nvidia ( NVDA ) and weighing up whether the selling pressure which is taking place in other high-flying stocks is likely to also take place at Apple?
And the answer is that realistically, in the short term, no one can give an accurate answer to this question. Although, that will not stop many from voicing their opinions and offering an answer. Having said that, over time, earnings power matters and valuation matters too - and Apple has both of these in its favor.
Investors Need To Focus On The Broad Portfolio The main takeaway from Apple's Q4 2018 earnings call is that Apple is going to be less reliant on new iterations of iPhones to drive forward the Apple's financial performance.
In fact, CFO Luca Maestri feels that going forward the best way to demonstrate the importance of its Services segment to the investment community, will be to highlight to investors Apple's Services gross margin contribution to Apple's consolidated gross margin.
In other words, starting with Apple's fiscal Q1 2019 a lot more emphasis will be made to highlight how successful Apple has been with its Services business. How Apple had the goal back in 2016 to double its revenues from its Services business by the end of 2020 to $50 billion. And how now, as of this latest quarter, Apple's Services business has reached $37 billion over its trailing twelve months. Thus, with the accounting adjustment aside, Apple's Services grew by an impressive 27% YoY, which implies, that even at a slightly slower run rate, Services should easily cross into the $50 billion revenue range by the end of fiscal 2020.
Catalyst For The Stock - It's All In The Price It is my contention, that in the near term, once investors stop focusing on iPhones sales, but more on Apple's revenue and bottom line profitability, Apple's share price will more accurately reflect its fundamental earnings power.
In fact, I get the sense that CEO Tim Cook and Maestri will see to it that investors start focusing a lot more on the fact that iPhones are only a gateway to Apple's broad portfolio of products and services.
For instance, what will further drive forward Apple's revenue over time will be Apple's ability to monetize its installed base on its major product categories - that's what ultimately will drive Apple's valuation.
Apple has in the past shown tremendous prowess in both accurately and highly pricing its product. Apple's unrelenting focus on pricing its products is so thoroughly ingrained in the company's culture. One can see this in Apple's brand, which always leaves consumers reaching for more (and deeper into their wallets), with its heavily priced lineup products, which consumers feel pressured to buy into, in order to participate in Apple's ecosystem.
For example, Apple's Group FaceTime is yet another way to keep consumers attracted to the convenience of easily interacting with a large number of family members and friends without having to be tech-savvy. In a modern world, who truly has the time to find apps which are able to reliably offer this service for free? Even if one member of the group has the time, the odds are that others won't have the time. Consequently, in an increasingly global society, this app will make users' life a little easier; consumers only have to be willing to pay the heavy price tag for Apple's major products to participate.
Valuation When all is said and done, it all boils down to Apple's attractive valuation. Sure, Apple is not the only tech company which has seen its share price fall of late. However, my argument is that certain companies will return to their former glory quicker than others.
Source: Author's calculations, morningstar.com
On the face of it, one could argue that Amazon ( AMZN ) is not a direct competitor to Apple, which is partially true, although only superficially. When we dig a little deeper, we can immediately understand how both companies are optimizing their services and products to be increasingly sticky. Amazon does this through its Prime offering, while Apple does it more subtly. Nevertheless, both corporations have, more which makes them similar rather than makes them different.
And right way, comparing these two tech titans, in Amazon's case, we can see how although it is priced roughly around $80 billion cheaper than Apple, or at a 10% discount to Apple, Amazon's valuation is significantly more stretched when compared with Apple's valuation.
Furthermore, as we have spent some time highlighting throughout the article, going forward, Apple's revenue will be increasingly reliant on its very high margin Services business, which will have significantly less need for CapEx. In other words, Apple's cash flows from operations will continue to be increasingly more valuable over time . And yet it's priced at nearly a third of the mighty capital intensive Amazon.
Takeaway Apple Services continues to grow at a rapid clip, yet investors are not fully appreciating how going forward, it will be Apple's Services which will drive forward Apple's share price. And finally, how Apple has become meaningfully undervalued during this tech sell-off.
